question: Does the unchanged P6AV registration and P6AT coherence protocol pass on a wholly different, higher-feature-count 1905 Barnard glass plate scanned in normal and perpendicular orientations?

primary_sources.title: SCORPION: A Multi-Scanner Whole-Slide Image Dataset for Cross-Scanner Analysis
Digitization, Measurement, and Analysis of a 1905 Barnard Atlas Photographic Plate

source.container: two IFDs: full-resolution primary RGB16 plus one reduced-resolution thumbnail

pre_score_source_amendments: The first attempt stopped on the official two-IFD container before registration; the contract then bound primary IFD zero and the reduced thumbnail IFD.
The second attempt stopped on RGB16 rather than grayscale before registration; an equal-weight integer RGB luminance rule was frozen before any registration or coherence score.

next_hypothesis: Stop SIFT threshold or crop rescue on these perpendicular scans. A further material-versus-scanner separation leaf requires source-provided correspondence or a genuinely different registration observation frozen on a fresh population.
claim_ceiling: one CC-BY-4.0 1905 glass astronomical plate scanned twice at perpendicular orientations; registration-source negative only, not isolated photographic-film NPS, scanner calibration, modern stock transfer or product evidence.
